review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the PiTensorProduct reindex simp lemmas. I also checked the downstream uses in TensorAlgebra/ToTensorPower.lean and the analogous tprod_mul_tprod in RingTheory/PiTensorProduct.lean. The simp attributes on cast_refl, cast_symm, cast_trans and cast_cast look consistent, and I found no cycle. I did not run Lean. The suggestions below about how simp would behave once the attributes are added are not tested. In particular, I did not check how the proposed cast_tprod would interact with cast_refl and Fin.cast simp lemmas when i = i. I judged gOne_def, gMul_def, cast_eq_cast and algebraMap₀_eq_smul_one to be deliberately left non-simp, and I did not report them.

findings.excerpt: cast R M h (tprod R a) = tprod R (a ∘ Fin.cast h.symm) :=
findings.problem: The other lemmas about `cast` (`cast_refl`, `cast_symm`, `cast_trans`, `cast_cast`) are `@[simp]`, and so is the underlying `reindex_tprod`. `cast_tprod` is the only rule that says how `cast` acts on a pure tensor, and it is not simp. Simp can therefore normalise compositions of casts but cannot push a cast through `tprod`, which leaves goals stuck. The file itself and the downstream file call it by hand: `simp only [..., tprod_mul_tprod, cast_tprod]` in `mul_assoc`, and `rw [TensorPower.cast_tprod]` in `list_prod_gradedMonoid_mk_single`. The rewrite is terminating, because the RHS contains no `cast`. It is also a plain simplification, replacing the cast by a reindexing of the arguments.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `cast_tprod` as `@[simp]`, alongside `cast_refl`, `cast_symm` and `cast_trans`. Then drop it from the explicit `simp only` lists where it is no longer needed. Before committing, check that the cases with `i = i` still normalise through `cast_refl` or `Fin.cast` simp lemmas.
findings.benefit: Casted pure tensors would normalise to `tprod R (a ∘ Fin.cast _)` automatically. The `cast` simp set would then cover every constructor of the interface, and proofs such as `one_mul` and `mul_assoc` would need fewer manual lemma lists.

findings.excerpt: tprod R a ₜ* tprod R b = tprod R (Fin.append a b) := by
findings.problem: This is the canonical evaluation rule for the graded multiplication on pure tensors. The analogous `PiTensorProduct.tprod_mul_tprod` in RingTheory/PiTensorProduct.lean is `@[simp]`, but this one is not. Every use is a manual `simp only [... tprod_mul_tprod ...]` or `rw [tprod_mul_tprod ..]`. The product can be unfolded to `mulEquiv (a ⊗ₜ b)` only through `gMul_def`, which is also not simp, so simp has no way to evaluate `tprod R a ₜ* tprod R b`. The rewrite terminates and moves towards a normal form, `tprod` of `Fin.append`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `tprod_mul_tprod`. Because the statement is written with the local `ₜ*` notation, it is already stated on `GradedMonoid.GMul.mul`, so it is a usable simp lemma for that head symbol. A companion statement for the `GradedMonoid.mk n a * GradedMonoid.mk m b` form could also be offered. `GradedMonoid.mk_mul_mk` already reduces that form to the `GMul.mul` form, and the `list_prod_gradedMonoid_mk_single` proof does exactly this rewrite chain by hand.
findings.benefit: Proofs about products of pure tensors would be handled by `simp`. The manual `rw`/`simp only` chains in `one_mul`, `mul_one`, `mul_assoc` and `list_prod_gradedMonoid_mk_single` would be shorter. Users would get the same behaviour as for the ring-valued `PiTensorProduct.tprod_mul_tprod`.
